subject: Channel & Marketplace Compliance — AWS/Azure/GCP detailed questionnaire
messages:
From: Sara Harrison <sara.harrison@enterpriseco.com>

Cc: laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, procurement <procurement@enterpriseco.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Marketplace channel compliance questionnaire (AWS/Azure/GCP) — deadline 11/20

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement at EnterpriseCo asked me to consolidate a detailed marketplace/commercial compliance questionnaire across the three major cloud marketplaces (AWS, Azure, GCP). The goal is to validate billing model compatibility, metering & usage reporting, private offer flows, and contract/purchase order expectations.

Can Redwood provide the following by EOD 2026-11-20?

  - A mapping of our SaaS billing model to marketplace metering (per-seat, monthly active, token-based) for AWS, Azure, GCP
  - Evidence of commercial flows: invoice, settlement cadence, and who owns the customer invoice (marketplace vs vendor)
  - Any required seller entitlements, marketplace technical integrations (metering endpoints, license keys, SaaS subscription APIs)
  - Standard contract/legal constraints for private offers and marketplace-managed discounts
  - Security & audit artifacts they typically request for listing (we already have SOC2 but they want flow examples specific to marketplaces)

I realize this is detailed — if you prefer we can take a phased delivery (technical + metering first, legal/commercial summary second). Looping Laura for product/ops detail.

Best,
Sara
Sara Harrison
Senior Sourcing Manager, EnterpriseCo

--

Subject: Re: Marketplace channel compliance questionnaire (AWS/Azure/GCP) — draft plan

Sara — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. We can deliver a phased pack as you suggested. Proposed plan:

Phase 1 (by 11/19):
- Metering & billing mapping for AWS/Azure/GCP (spreadsheet)
- Technical integration checklist (metering endpoints, subscription APIs, sample payloads)

Phase 2 (by 11/23):
- Commercial/legal playbook for private offers & settlement flows (short memo + common contract clauses)
- Security evidence summary specific to marketplace onboarding (SOC2 references + sample audit logs and retention notes)

Internal asks / owners:
- Laura: lead meter/billing mapping and provide metering matrix (I can review)
- Karthik: draft the technical integration checklist and example API payloads
- Monica: pull legal/commercial bullet points and coordinate with Legal for any required language

I'll assemble the Phase 1 artifacts and send a consolidated zip. Laura — can you take the owner for the metering matrix? Karthik/Monica, please confirm.

Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:26:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace channel compliance questionnaire (AWS/Azure/GCP) — Phase 1 deliverables attached

Sara / team — attaching Phase 1 deliverables for your review. Highlights below:

Attachments included:
- Redwood_Marketplace_RFI_Draft_v1.pdf (detailed answers to your questionnaire rows)
- metering_and_billing_matrix.xlsx (per-cloud mapping: how our token & session billing maps to marketplace metering options)
- legal_commercial_summary.docx (high level summary; Legal will follow up on any contract redlines)

Key points (summary):
- Metering: For AWS and GCP we support a token-based usage meter (push-based usage records or meter SaaS subscription tiers). For Azure Marketplace we recommend the SaaS subscription model or meter via ARM-based metering hooks — see sheet 'CloudNotes' for required endpoints.
- Invoice ownership: Redwood prefers vendor-billed model for direct contracts; marketplaces can be configured for vendor invoice or marketplace invoice. For EnterpriseCo's procurement needs, we recommend vendor-billed private offer for clearer invoicing and faster settlement.
- Private offers: All three marketplaces support private offer flows; differences are in UI & legal annexes. We'll include sample language for private-offer acceptance and termination windows in Phase 2.
- Security artifacts: We included pointers to SOC 2 report and a short note on audit logging policies and retention (we store request-level logs for 90 days by default; extended retention is configurable).

Next steps:
1) Sara — can you confirm if vendor-billed private offer is acceptable? That will determine the contract path.
2) Markus / Monica / Karthik — Legal will likely want to review the commercial summary; I'll open a shared drive folder for comments.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Laura Bennett
Product Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference

--

Subject: Re: Marketplace channel compliance questionnaire (AWS/Azure/GCP) — received, next steps

Laura / Markus — received, thank you. The Phase 1 artifacts are very helpful and cover the majority of internal procurement follow-ups. A few clarifying notes from procurement:

  - Vendor-billed private offer is acceptable and preferred for our finance team (keeps invoicing clean).
  - For AWS: can you include an example usage-file format (CSV/JSON) for token-based metering we can validate against our ingestion?
  - For Azure: procurement asks about billing reconciliation timelines — do you have an expected settlement window for marketplace-managed vs vendor-managed billing?
  - For GCP: we want a short note on publisher verification steps and any required seller attestation.

Procurement will review Phase 1 this week and expects Phase 2 deliverables by 11/23 so Legal can start their review. I'll also loop AWS Marketplace ops separately for any platform-specific checks.

Sara
Sara Harrison
Senior Sourcing Manager, EnterpriseCo
